summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported that Tom Allen was charged with second-degree murder for killing Timothy Confoy and released on $5,000 bond, after a coroner's jury returned a verdict of justifiable homicide.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Wednesday Morning, March 1, 1899, page 12.

facts.fact: A coroner's jury returned a verdict of justifiable homicide in the killing of Timothy Confoy at Allen's saloon after about ten minutes; Allen made no statement on his attorney's advice
At the request of his attorney, ex-Judge Thomas B. Harvey, Allen was charged with second-degree murder so he could be released on bond, and was freed on $5,000 bond signed by attorney Thomas J. Rowe

Inquest evidence: a revolver was found under Confoy's body, which L. G. Perry, a member of the Legislature, said Confoy had borrowed from him; witnesses said Confoy had threatened to 'clean out' Allen's place
